name: 1st Place Medal
description: A gold medal, given to the person or team who comes first in a competitive sporting event such as a race.
1st Place Medal was approved as part of Unicode 9.0 in 2016 under the name "First Place Medal" and added to Emoji 3.0 in 2016.

name: B Button (Blood Type)
description: A symbol representing Blood Type B. Displayed as the letter B on a red background. Sometimes used online to replace the letter C at the start of words in reference to the Bloods street gang's practice of turning words like cool into bool . This has expanded in some instances to starting any word with the letter B, or more specifically, this emoji which makes it more 🅱️lear that a letter has been replaced. Samsung's design for this emoji previously included a blue background instead of a red background.
B Button (Blood Type) was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Negative Squared Latin Capital Letter B" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: CL Button
description: The letters “CL” typically displayed on a red or pink square background. "CL" was used as an abbreviation on the “clear” button featured commonly on mobile phones during the late 1990s through the mid-2000s. Facebook's design has an orange background, though it was previously red . Google's background was previously yellow , while Samsung's was light blue . This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by Docomo in 1999 .
CL Button was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Squared CL" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

Flag: Guadeloupe was added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

While a 1949 decree specified that the flag’s stripes should be cyan, in practice they remained dark blue for nearly seventy years, until 2022. As of December 2024, most major vendors display the emoji’s stripes in a shade of blue darker than cyan.
The Flag: Honduras emoji is a flag sequence combining 🇭 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter H and 🇳 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter N . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Honduras was added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: ID Button
description: The letters “ID” shown on a square button. Typically depicted as white letters on a purple square, though colors vary by platform. See also: 🪪 Identification Card . This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by Softbank and Docomo in 1999.
ID Button was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Squared ID" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Japanese “Application” Button
description: This Emoji has two meanings. One meaning is “request” in Japanese. An alternative meaning is “monkey” in the Chinese zodiac. It is commonly used in Japan to denote an application form or contact information for inquiries. CJK Ideographs are characters used in Chinese, Japanese and Korean languages. Their writing systems all completely or partly use Chinese characters .
Japanese “Application” Button was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Squared CJK Unified Ideograph-7533" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Japanese Dolls
description: Ornamental Japanese Emperor and Empress dolls, as displayed in celebration of Hinamatsuri on March 3 in Japan (Girls’ or Dolls’ Day). Generally depicted as a Japanese Emperor (left, in blue, holding a scepter) and Empress (right, in red, holding a fan) in ceremonial court dress and seated on a tatami. When not applied to Hinamatsuri , sometimes used to represent Japan, dolls, a pair of people (as a couple or two friends), and for various idiosyncratic purposes.
Japanese Dolls was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Japanese “Service Charge” Button
description: A square button bearing the Katakana character サ (“sa”). This is an abbreviation of sābisu-ryō (サービス料), meaning “service charge,” and is commonly used in Japan to indicate something complimentary or free of charge, such as a drink given “on the house” to a regular customer. Most platforms display the button in blue or gray, though Facebook’s is red. Various early Google designs were orange .
Japanese “Service Charge” Button was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Squared Katakana Sa" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Japanese Symbol for Beginner
description: A yellow and green shield symbol, called a Shoshinsha Mark . Must be displayed by drivers in Japan for one year after they receive their driving licence. Similar to L-Plates used to identify learner drivers in other countries. Known to be used to reference sports teams with yellow and green as their colors, such as Norwich City FC or the Green Bay Packers. Similarly, it can be used to represent additional concepts associated with the same color combination.
Japanese Symbol for Beginner was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Flag: Kyrgyzstan
description: The flag for Kyrgyzstan , which may show as the letters KG on some platforms. In late 2023, this flag was updated to straighten the previously wavy sun rays radiating from its center. However, as of December 2024, no major emoji vendor has adjusted their designs to reflect this change. It’s possible they may not do so at all, given that such a subtle alteration would be nearly indistinguishable at the typical small sizes in which emojis are displayed.
The Flag: Kyrgyzstan emoji is a flag sequence combining 🇰 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter K and 🇬 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter G . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Kyrgyzstan was added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Mx Claus
description: A person, generally depicted as being older with gray hair, wearing a red Christmas (aka "Santa") hat. Does not represent any specific character in folklore. Mx Claus provides a gender inclusive alternative to 🎅 Santa Claus or 🤶 Mrs. Claus . Apple, Huawei, and Toss Face depict Mx Claus as wearing glasses , while other vendors do not. Mx is an honorific that does not indicate gender .
The Mx Claus emoji is a ZWJ sequence combining 🧑 Person , Zero Width Joiner and 🎄 Christmas Tree . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Mx Claus was added to Emoji 13.0 in 2020.

New Caledonia is an overseas territory of France, and before 2010 the French flag was the sole emblem representing the territory. However, in July 2010, the New Caledonian Congress supported flying the Kanak people's flag of the FLNKS independence movement alongside the French flag . It is this Kanak flag design that all emoji vendors use for the New Caledonia emoji flag sequence.
The Flag: New Caledonia emoji is a flag sequence combining 🇳 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter N and 🇨 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter C . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: New Caledonia was added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: OK Hand
description: A gesture showing the index finger and thumb touching to make an open circle. Represents “I’m okay” or “yes, that’s correct / good”. In American Sign Language (ASL), the number nine is represented with this gesture. The same hand sign can be seen as offensive in some cultures, including in parts of Europe, the Middle East, and South America. This can also be used as a symbol of White Supremacy , depending on context.
OK Hand was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "OK Hand Sign" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Soon Arrow
description: The word “SOON” capitalized with an arrow above it, pointing to the right. Typically used to indicate something upcoming or happening shortly. Huawei and Google place the arrow and text inside a blue square background, as did a previous Microsoft design . An early Google design lacked the square background and had an orange arrow . This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by Docomo in 1999 .
Soon Arrow was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Soon with Rightwards Arrow Above" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Santa Claus
description: Santa Claus, sometimes referred to as Father Christmas , brings joy to children at Christmas time. Displayed with a beard and red festive hat. The Santa emoji had a frown on Android 4.4 , which was resolved in Android 5.0. See also: Christmas emoji list . Note: Father Christmas has a different origin to Santa Claus but both are represented by this single emoji.
Santa Claus was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Father Christmas" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Flag: Sark
description: The “exceptionally reserved” ISO 3166 code for Sark , which may show as the letters CQ on some platforms. The flag for Sark was the first flag emoji sequence using two-letter ISO codes to be recommended by Unicode since they first formally approved emoji flags through Emoji 1.0 back in 2015.
The Flag: Sark emoji is a flag sequence combining 🇨 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter C and 🇶 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter Q . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Sark was added to Emoji 16.0 in 2024.

name: Flag: Scotland
description: The flag for Scotland, a country in the United Kingdom . May show as the letters gbsct. WhatsApp also recognizes the flag using a non-standard flag sequence that combines the 🇽 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter X and 🇸 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter S , even though this pairing is not part of ISO 3166-1

The Flag: Scotland emoji is a tag sequence combining 🏴 Black Flag , 󠁧 Tag Latin Small Letter G , 󠁢 Tag Latin Small Letter B , 󠁳 Tag Latin Small Letter S , 󠁣 Tag Latin Small Letter C , 󠁴 Tag Latin Small Letter T and 󠁿 Cancel Tag . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Scotland was added to Emoji 5.0 in 2017.

name: Statue of Liberty
description: The Statue of Liberty , often used as a depiction of New York City . Due to its initial inclusion in an early Japanese emoji set , it is possible that this emoji was originally intended to represent the recreation of the Statue of Liberty located on the Odaiba island in Tokyo Bay.
Statue of Liberty was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

Unlike most global flags, it is square instead of rectangular. Initially most vendors displayed this flag as a rectangle, consistent with other emoji flags, but today the majority of vendors display the flag with its accurate real-world shape.
The Flag: Switzerland emoji is a flag sequence combining 🇨 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter C and 🇭 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter H . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Switzerland was added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Flag: Syria
description: The flag for Syria , which may show as the letters SY on some platforms. As of April 2025, this emoji shows the flag of Syrian National Coalition (a horizontal triband of green, white, and black, with three red five-pointed stars on the white band) on updated Apple and Samsung devices, as well as within WhatsApp on Android. Other vendors are expected to follow suit in the future . Many other vendors still display this emoji as the flag of the Syrian Arab Republic (a horizontal triabnd of red, white, and black; charged with two green stars at the centre).
The Flag: Syria emoji is a flag sequence combining 🇸 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter S and 🇾 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter Y . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Syria was added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: T-Rex
description: A Tyrannosaurus rex, a massive, meat-eating dinosaur with huge jaws, tiny arms, and a long tail. Depicted as a green tyrannosaur standing on its hind lefts facing left, often with a textured back, sharp teeth, and clawed toes. May be used to represent various dinosaurs, including raptors. See also 🦕 Sauropod . May also be used to call a person a dinosaur, i.e. imply that they are old-fashioned or out-of-touch with modern sentiments. Available as an Apple Animoji . Google’s T-rex used to look somewhat like a velociraptor, though the design has since changed. Samsung’s T-Rex was previously red, Microsoft's brown, and Facebook’s only a green head with open jaws.
T-Rex was approved as part of Unicode 10.0 in 2017 and added to Emoji 5.0 in 2017.

name: Top Arrow
description: The word “TOP” capitalized with an arrow above it, pointing upward. Can be used to indicate the top of a page, list, screen, or ranking, or to return to the beginning of content. Huawei and Google place the arrow and text inside a square background, as did a previous Microsoft design . Apple's initial design also featured a square background but did not include an arrow. An early Google design lacked the square background and had a yellow arrow . This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by SoftBank in 1999 .
Top Arrow was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Top with Upwards Arrow Above" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Flag: Taiwan
description: The flag for Taiwan (officially Republic of China ), which may show as the letters TW on some platforms. This Taiwanese flag is hidden from the emoji keyboard on iOS devices when the region is set to China mainland or (as of iOS 13.1.2) Hong Kong or Macau. Chinese-model iPhones will not display this emoji and will instead show a missing character tofu (☒) in place of the flag, as will iOS devices with region set to China mainland . Hong Kong and Macua only hide this emoji from the emoji keyboard . This emoji is also not available within emoji set created by Chinese mobile manufacturer Huawei - it will render as a blank space.
The Flag: Taiwan emoji is a flag sequence combining 🇹 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter T and 🇼 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter W . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Taiwan was added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Flag: Wales
description: The flag for Wales, a country in the United Kingdom . May show as the letters gbwls. WhatsApp also recognizes the flag using a non-standard flag sequence that combines the 🇽 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter X and 🇼 Regional Indicator Symbol Letter W , even though this pairing is not part of ISO 3166-1

The Flag: Wales emoji is a tag sequence combining 🏴 Black Flag , 󠁧 Tag Latin Small Letter G , 󠁢 Tag Latin Small Letter B , 󠁷 Tag Latin Small Letter W , 󠁬 Tag Latin Small Letter L , 󠁳 Tag Latin Small Letter S and 󠁿 Cancel Tag . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Flag: Wales was added to Emoji 5.0 in 2017.

name: Zzz
description: Three “Z” characters forming “Zzz,” a visual metaphor from comics and cartoons used to represent light snoring while sleeping, as in the phrase “ catching some Zs. ” Can be used to represent sleeping, snoring, dreaming, or any sleep-related state. Can also be used in some contexts to represent something that is boring (slang, snooze ). Typically shown in shades of blue, though Facebook’s and Huawei’s designs use purple.
Zzz was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Sleeping Symbol" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Abacus
description: An abacus , an ancient tool used to count and calculate by moving beads. Depicted as a wooden frame with four or more rows or columns of variously positioned and colored beads. Used for various content concerning mathematics and science (education) as well as calculations, counting, and numbers more generally. Designs from Apple, Google, and Facebook resemble a Chinese abacus ( suanpan ), as did a previous Microsoft design. By one reckoning, Apple’s red-beaded design displays the number 108 and Emojipedia's, 12,031,981.
Abacus was approved as part of Unicode 11.0 in 2018 and added to Emoji 11.0 in 2018.

name: Accordion
description: A red accordion with a keyboard on one side, buttons on the other side, and bellows in the middle. Used to talk about accordion music or music in general. Also may be used in reference to things that expand and contract, or are folded like the bellows of an accordion.
Accordion was approved as part of Unicode 13.0 in 2020 and added to Emoji 13.0 in 2020.

Admission Tickets was approved as part of Unicode 7.0 in 2014 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Admission Tickets
description: A ticket to an event, shown with perforated edges and typically bearing the text “Admit One” on the front. Displayed in red or pink on most platforms, though WhatsApp’s design is yellow and Huawei’s is blue. A previous Google design displayed two blue tickets. LG’s design also showed two yellow tickets, though that set has since been discontinued . See also: 🎫 Ticket .
Admission Tickets was approved as part of Unicode 7.0 in 2014 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Aerial Tramway
description: An Aerial Tramway, most commonly seen at ski resorts, for transport between locations on a mountain . Can also be used as a tourist attraction, or as a form of public transport. In 2018 this emoji was the focus of a grassroots campaign on Twitter (now X) where users of the platform began using this emoji more frequently. This was to update the least-used emoji on emojitracker.com (as tracked by the @leastUsedEmoji Twitter bot) from the Aerial Tramway to another emoji. In May 2025 this emoji was also used within YouTube comments to signify laughter or approval or to create confusion for people not in the know. This was an emulation of what occurred with the 🪑 Chair emoji in 2021, which you can learn about here . Given its historically low usage, this emoji was featured in a March 2026 Saturday Night Live (SNL) “Weekend Update” segment, where it was described as “the number one least used emoji.”
Aerial Tramway was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Airplane
description: A large passenger aircraft, typically shown from above and facing toward the upper right. Wing colors and the number of engines vary by platform. Often used to represent air travel, including overseas vacations. May also be used as a proxy for airplane mode on a phone or tablet, or figuratively to express a desire to escape far away from a situation. Use of this emoji declined in April 2020 , likely as a result of global air travel limitations.
Airplane was approved as part of Unicode 1.1 in 1993 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Airplane Arrival
description: A large passenger plane approaching a runway for landing. Typically shown facing right with its nose angled toward the ground, sometimes appearing steeper than a real-world landing approach. However, the angle and perspective vary by platform, as do the plane model and color. Previous designs from Microsoft and Facebook omitted the runway, instead depicting the plane among clouds or above a green landmass, respectively.
Airplane Arrival was approved as part of Unicode 7.0 in 2014 under the name "Airplane Arriving" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Alembic
description: An apparatus for distilling, as used in medieval alchemy . Generally depicted as a round flask with a neck angled down to the right. Positioned on a short stand and containing a mysterious green, purple, or blue liquid. Commonly used for various content concerning chemistry and science more generally. May represent various liquids, such as potions or medicines, as well as metaphorical laboratories and experiments. Thanks to the alembic’s association with alchemy, this emoji may also convey a sense of magic. And, thanks to its resemblance to a glass pipe, some use the emoji to represent a bong or other drug paraphernalia. Samsung’s design previously featured a copper still, as used for making whiskey .
Alembic was approved as part of Unicode 4.1 in 2005 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Alien
description: A classic alien face. The oval, bare head of a gray or green alien with large black eyes and a slight, friendly smile. Samsung depicts nostrils, Facebook a nose. May represent extraterrestrial life or topics concerning outer space, but commonly conveys a playful sense of weirdness or strangeness, as if someone or something is out there or from another planet . Available as an Apple Animoji . Animated variants from Google and JoyPixels depict the alien flashing a ✌️ Peace Sign gesture, as if to say, “I come in peace.” Apple previously displayed a similar looking alien head in a box as a placeholder for an unknown emoji, but now shows a boxed question mark.
Alien was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Extraterrestrial Alien" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Alien Monster
description: A friendly-looking, tentacled space creature with two eyes. Most major platforms style their design after aliens in classic arcade games like Space Invaders , rendering it purple and pixellated, as if in 8-bit graphics. May be used of topics concerning extraterrestrial life, outer space, gaming, and computing, but also enjoys a range of idiosyncratic applications, such as conveying a sense of weirdness, wackiness, or excitement, given that the emoji looks like it is raising its arms shouting Yay! on many platforms. May also be used to reference the streaming platform Twitch , given that the emoji’s color resembles the Twitch logo and both are strongly linked to gaming culture. WhatsApp uses this emoji in push notifications to indicate a text message containing a GIF. Samsung’s design previously resembled an octopus , with an even earlier Samsung design featuring a big-brained alien , à la Star Trek . Earlier designs from Google and Microsoft depicted more cartoon-like alien monsters.
Alien Monster was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

Amphora was approved as part of Unicode 8.0 in 2015 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Angry Face with Horns
description: A purple face with two devil horns, a frowning mouth, and eyes and eyebrows scrunched downwards in anger. Bears the same expression as 😠 Angry Face and 😡 Pouting Face on most platforms. Commonly used to represent devils and devilish behavior, especially around Halloween . It is also used to convey various sentiments of anger or ideas of evil. More menacing than its 😈 Smiling Face With Horns counterpart. Facebook’s design has black horns, green eyes, and clenched teeth. Several early vendor designs more closely aligned with this emoji’s original Unicode name, Imp , a term referring to a small demon in folklore. Samsung previously depicted a childlike character with red hair and horns, fangs, and black wings. Earlier designs from Google featured an orangish-red character with blue hair and wings.
Angry Face with Horns was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Imp" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Anguished Face
description: A face with small, open eyes, open frown, and raised eyebrows. Bears the same eyes and mouth as 😦 Frowning Face With Open Mouth on most platforms, but its eyebrows give it a more surprised expression. Meaning widely varies, but may convey alarm, confusion, or sadness, as if gasping in shock or concern. A previous Samsung design showed upper teeth and a visible tongue, while an even earlier version depicted a visible breath of air being expelled, similar to the later-introduced 😮‍💨 Face Exhaling emoji. Microsoft’s original design featured scrunched eyes resembling those of the 😖 Confounded Face and 😣 Persevering Face emojis, while Google’s included a single bead of sweat, similar to the 😓 Downcast Face with Sweat and 😥 Sad but Relieved Face emojis.
Anguished Face was approved as part of Unicode 6.1 in 2012 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Ant
description: An ant, a small, industrious insect that lives in a colony. Depicted as a black or red ant, typically in full profile on its six legs facing left, with a prominent abdomen and antennae . May be used to represent ants specifically, as well as various insects or other bugs . As such, it may also be used for metaphorical senses of bug , such as a software error, an annoyance (e.g. a "bugbear"), a hidden listening device, or an enthusiasm (e.g. “catching the travel bug"). Facebook’s ant is red, as was a previous Microsoft design. Google’s ant was previously blue, and Facebook’s was previously black. This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by au by KDDI in 2000 .
Ant was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Antenna Bars
description: Bars increasing in height, as displayed on a mobile phone to indicate the strength of a cellular or wireless network signal. More bars signify better reception. Typically depicted as a white series of bars on a blue square background, though Google and Samsung’s backgrounds are orange and Facebook’s is green. The number of bars shown varies slightly by platform, though all platforms depict full signal strength. Many previous designs from several platforms, including Google , Samsung , Microsoft , and Facebook , also included an antenna symbol placed beside the bars. This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by au by KDDI in 2003 .
Antenna Bars was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Antenna with Bars" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Anxious Face with Sweat
description: A face with open eyes and a small, open frown. Its eyebrows are furrowed, with a single bead of cold sweat dripping down, and its forehead is pale blue, as if experiencing a cold flash. Samsung's design shows upper teeth and tongue. Meaning widely varies, but commonly conveys such feelings as sadness, disappointment, fear, and anxiety. Similar to 😥 Sad but Relieved Face , but with a blue head and larger frown. Not to be confused with 😢 Crying Face , 😪 Sleepy Face , or other emojis with tear or sweat droplets. Microsoft and Samsung previously featured smileys that appeared more excited in expression.
Anxious Face with Sweat was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Face with Open Mouth and Cold Sweat" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Artist Palette
description: An artist’s palette , used to hold and mix paint colors while painting. Typically depicted as a wooden palette with four to six blobs of paint, often in colors such as red, blue, green, yellow, or purple, and a thumb hole. Commonly used to represent art, painting, arts and crafts, and other creative pursuits. An early Microsoft design also included a paintbrush .
Artist Palette was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Astonished Face
description: A yellow face with open eyes, raised eyebrows, and an open mouth, as if gasping in shock or surprise. Often depicted showing its upper teeth. May convey a wide range of emotions, including awe, amazement, admiration, disbelief, excitement, or concern. Similar to 😯 Hushed Face , which features smaller eyes and mouth. Several earlier designs, including Apple’s , displayed X-shaped eyes, making the emoji resemble 😵 Dizzy Face . Google’s design previously depicted a wobbly expression, as if inebriated . Huawei's design for this emoji includes a 💥 Collision -like symbol behind its head, emphasising its astonishment.
Astonished Face was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Baby
description: The face of a baby with a small tuft of hair on top of its head. Some platforms show the baby sucking on a pacifier, and some platforms show a single tooth in the baby’s open mouth. Android previously displayed this emoji as a swaddled baby. On Snapchat , the baby emoji signifies a new friend on the service. This emoji can also be used in the context of the meme “I’m baby.” See also 👼 Baby Angel .
Baby was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Baby Angel
description: A baby with a halo and wings. Can represent a sweet baby, a biblical cherub, a mythological cupid, a decorative putto, or an angel as a supernatural being in general. This emoji can be used earnestly or in a tongue-in-cheek way to talk about goodness or innocence. It is often used to express affection for people, especially children at birth or, more sadly, after death. This emoji pops up in a large variety of contexts ranging from innocence, love, Valentine's Day, positive feelings like gratitude, and the Christian faith, especially during Christmas . See also 👶 Baby .
Baby Angel was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Baby Chick
description: A yellow baby chicken (chick). Variously depicted as a chick in full profile, standing on its legs, or as a chick head. Both designs show the bird facing left, with an orange beak and feet. Often used with an affectionate tone. May be used to represent various types of baby birds. May also be used to represent chicken foods (e.g., poultry , eggs ), spring , Easter , or slang senses of chick . Not to be confused with 🐣 Hatching Chick or 🐥Front-Facing Baby Chick , though their applications overlap. See also 🐔 Chicken and 🐓 Rooster . Apple, WhatsApp, Huawei, and Facebook’s designs feature a chick head; other major platforms display a full-bodied chick.
Baby Chick was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Baby Symbol
description: The symbol for a baby, usually used to indicate a room suitable for changing a baby. Often located in or near public restrooms . Typically depicted as a simplified white baby silhouette wearing a diaper on an orange or blue square background. Most platforms show the baby seated facing forward with arms and legs outstretched, while Apple and WhatsApp instead depict a crawling baby in profile. An early Google design displayed a yellow baby figure wearing a diaper, as did Facebook's initial design . Another Facebook design previously depicted the baby as crawling in profile , while a Microsoft design previously had a red background . This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by SoftBank in 1999 .
Baby Symbol was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Backhand Index Pointing Left
description: An index finger pointing to the left. Since 2020 this emoji has been known to be combined with the 🥺 Pleading Face and the 👉 Backhand Index Pointing Right to indicate a bashful or shy pose (🥺👉👈), also often called a "simp" pose. An alternative "simp" pose uses the 😔 Pensive Face (😔👉👈). Additionally, using the 🙄 Rolling Eyes in between the pointing finger emojis indicates a person dismissively plugging their ears in an "I'm not listening" gesture (👉🙄👈).
Backhand Index Pointing Left was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "White Left Pointing Backhand Index" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Backhand Index Pointing Right
description: An index finger pointing to the right. Since 2020 this emoji has been known to be combined with the 🥺 Pleading Face and the 👈 Backhand Index Pointing Left to indicate a bashful or shy pose (🥺👉👈), also often called a "simp" pose. An alternative "simp" pose uses the 😔 Pensive Face (😔👉👈). Additionally, using the 🙄 Rolling Eyes in between the pointing finger emojis indicates a person dismissively plugging their ears in an "I'm not listening" gesture (👉🙄👈).

Since 2020 this emoji has been known to be combined with the 🥺 Pleading Face and the 👈 Backhand Index Pointing Left to indicate a bashful or shy pose (🥺👉👈), also often called a "simp" pose. An alternative "simp" pose uses the 😔 Pensive Face (😔👉👈). Additionally, using the 🙄 Rolling Eyes in between the pointing finger emojis indicates a person dismissively plugging their ears in an "I'm not listening" gesture (👉🙄👈).
Backhand Index Pointing Right was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "White Right Pointing Backhand Index" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Backhand Index Pointing Up
description: Index finger pointing upward, showing the back of the hand while doing so. Often used to draw attention to text, a comment, or a link appearing above (‘see above’), or to emphasize agreement with a previous post (‘this,’ ‘facts’). May also be used playfully to reference oneself (‘that’s me’). In faith-based contexts, it can signify pointing toward heaven or giving thanks to God.
Backhand Index Pointing Up was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "White Up Pointing Backhand Index" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Balance Scale
description: A balance scale, as historically used to measure weight. A symbol of justice, as held by Lady Justice , and of the zodiac sign of Libra , the Scales. Depicted as two silver or gold pans suspended from a beam and supported on a base. Commonly used for various content concerning law and justice as well as various senses of balance and weight. Samsung’s design previously featured a stylized, white balance scale on a green square, as an icon or symbol of legal matters or institutions.
Balance Scale was approved as part of Unicode 4.1 in 2005 under the name "Scales" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Ballet Shoes
description: Shoes worn by ballet dancers for pointe work . As such, most platforms show a pair of pink or peach shoes resting en pointe, though WhatsApp only shows a single shoe, as did a previous Toss Face design . Sometimes used to represent dancing in general, rather than ballet specifically. Historically was occasionally used to represent the color pink, though this predated the introduction of the 🩷 Pink Heart . In September 2025 , a 🧑‍🩰 Ballet Dancer was approved, creating a gender-neutral alternative to the 💃 Woman Dancing and 🕺 Man Dancing emojis. Each of the skin tone variations of the 🧑‍🩰 Ballet Dancer are shown wearing ballet shoes matching their skin tone.
Ballet Shoes was approved as part of Unicode 12.0 in 2019 and added to Emoji 12.0 in 2019.

name: Ballot Box with Ballot
description: A ballot box, as used to cast votes in an election. Depicted as a box, generally blue or gray, with a slot on top through which a paper ballot is being inserted. Commonly used for various content concerning voting and elections, especially in politics and government. Several platforms display a cross mark or check mark on the ballot to indicate a vote, though Apple, Google, and Facebook leave theirs blank. WhatsApp includes two check marks , while Twitter’s design also shows multiple rows of selectable options. Two different previous Google designs featured a cross mark , as did early designs from Facebook , Microsoft , and Twitter .
Ballot Box with Ballot was approved as part of Unicode 7.0 in 2014 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Bank
description: A retail bank branch where people can perform money -related tasks. Also a common location to find an ATM . Generally depicted as a gray building with a large dollar sign above its door, though Huawei’s design shows a yuan symbol instead. Several previous designs from Google , Samsung , and Facebook included the word “bank” on the building before replacing it with a large dollar sign. In Japan, this emoji came to be associated with the slang term bakkureru (“to slack off” or evade responsibility), due to the “BK” letters used to represent this emoji in early Japanese emoji sets from Softbank and Docomo . Early Apple designs for this emoji also included the letters “BK.”
Bank was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Bar Chart
description: A bar graph generally showing three different-colored, vertical rectangles at various heights, as compares values across a category. Commonly used to represent various types of data, information, facts, figures, and charts more generally. Several platforms, including Apple, depict (left to right) a green, red (lowest), and blue bar (highest). Google’s design previously included four bars, with yellow being the highest.
Bar Chart was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Basket
description: A basket, as used for storing or carrying such things as food or clothes. Appearance widely varies across platforms but generally depicted as woven from wicker with one or more handles. Commonly used to represent doing laundry or having a picnic. Apple and WhatsApp’s designs, featuring a white cloth, suggest a bread or picnic basket. Microsoft’s design previously suggested a laundry basket by holding a blue garment or cloth. Samsung’s design previously displayed green fabric, as knitted from yarn . Not to be confused with 🗑️ Wastebasket .
Basket was approved as part of Unicode 11.0 in 2018 and added to Emoji 11.0 in 2018.

name: Bathtub
description: A white bathtub with a silver shower head. Often depicted as a cast-iron tub with claw-foot legs. Commonly used for various content concerning bathing, washing, cleaning, and bathrooms more generally. Several platforms, including Apple and Facebook, feature soap bubbles or suds. Samsung’s design displays streaming water from the shower head. Vendors implement 🛀 Person Taking a Bath with the same or a similar emoji, but with a person soaking in the tub.
Bathtub was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Battery
description: An electric battery, as used to power devices such as a flashlight . Generally depicted as an upright, green cylinder, as a AA or D cell , with white indicators for its positive (facing up) and negative terminals. Commonly used for various content concerning electricity, charging, energy, and power, especially in figurative senses. Its green color also suggests the icon for battery power on a cell/ mobile phone . Across social platforms in 2025, this emoji began to be used as a positive counterpart to the 🪫 Low Battery emoji, as part of a Gen Z trend of chaotically swapping through different emojis to express various emotional states. Apple’s design includes a voltage symbol ; WhatsApp’s battery is a blueish grey.
Battery was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Beans
description: Beans, as used in cuisines around the world. May be used to talk about food, flatulence (caused by eating beans), or coffee beans. Also used to discuss money, counting, or a small amount of something. May be used to refer to the head. Additionally may be used with phrases such as spill the beans , full of beans , or cool beans . This emoji is alluded to in the 2025 hit Netflix show Adolescence . Learn more here .
Beans was approved as part of Unicode 14.0 in 2021 and added to Emoji 14.0 in 2021.

name: Bear
description: A friendly, cartoon-styled face of bear, looking straight ahead. Depicted as a brown bear with round ears and a tan muzzle. Resembles a teddy bear . Often used with an affectionate tone. Does not have a full-bodied bear emoji counterpart. May be used to refer to certain members of the LGBTQ community, a la the slang term "bear". Available as an Apple Animoji . Samsung’s bear was previously golden brown.
Bear was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 under the name "Bear Face" and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Beaver
description: A brown beaver with buckteeth and a wide paddle-like tail. Can be used in the context of actual beavers, or metaphorically to evoke qualities of beavers like working hard, as in the expression beavering away . Commonly associated with Canada, as beavers are a national emblem of the country. May also be used in reference to the vagina, which is an informal sense of the word beaver .
Beaver was approved as part of Unicode 13.0 in 2020 and added to Emoji 13.0 in 2020.

name: Bed
description: A bed, made up for sleeping in a house , hotel , or other sleeping accommodation . Shown with a headboard at the left, footboard, mattress, pillow, and sheet. Most platforms suggest a wooden frame and feature blue or red sheets. Commonly used for various content concerning beds, furniture, and housing as well as sleeping , relaxing, and other bedroom activities. Vendors implement the same style of bed for 🛌 Person in Bed , but without a sleeper under the covers.
Bed was approved as part of Unicode 7.0 in 2014 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Bell
description: A gold or yellow bell, which is commonly used on mobile phones as an icon for notifications or ringing sounds. This emoji saw a spike in use after a 2015 Game of Thrones episode that featured a character ringing a bell and chanting “Shame!” while parading another through the streets. The scene became a popular meme, with this emoji still occasionally paired with the word “shame” to reference the moment and meme. This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by au by KDDI in 1999 .
Bell was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Beverage Box
description: Originally proposed as Juice , this emoji can be used to talk about juice or other liquids that come in boxes with straws. It can also be used metaphorically to describe power, energy, respect, or an elusive quality that makes someone special (i.e., "they've got the juice"). This emoji may be considered antisemitic in certain contexts, particularly when used to disparage, insult, or abuse individuals while attempting to circumvent content moderation on platforms such as TikTok. Such usage is based on a perceived phonetic similarity between "Jewish" and “juice.” While intended to be used to represent a broad selection of juices and other liquids, most vendors' designs feature a 🍎 Red Apple symbol. 🍇 Grapes , 🍊Tangerine , 🍑 Peach , 🍒 Cherries , 🍐 Pear , and a 🌞 Sun with Face across other more distinct designs.
Beverage Box was approved as part of Unicode 12.0 in 2019 and added to Emoji 12.0 in 2019.

name: Bikini
description: A two-piece bikini, worn at the beach, pool, or on vacation at a tropical destination . Shown in a variety of colors and patterns across different platforms: Apple, Google, Samsung, WhatsApp, and Microsoft use polka-dot patterns on pink, red, or purple material, with Apple's polka dots being yellow . Facebook has an orange striped design. Twitter shows a plain purple bikini, Huawei a plain orange one, and JoyPixels a plain teal one. Samsung’s earlier designs showed a striped string bikini, initially in blue and then purple . Previous Google designs were orange . One Microsoft design was previously red , and plain yellow before that. Facebook previously had a purple polka-dot bikini , and a plain red one before that. Related emojis include 🩲 Briefs , 🩳 Shorts , and 🩱 One-Piece Swimsuit . This emoji predates the inclusion of emojis within Unicode . It was first added to early Japanese emoji keyboards by SoftBank in 2000 .
Bikini was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Billed Cap
description: A plain soft hat with a rounded crown and a stiff bill. Most often shown in a shade of blue and displayed at an angle to clearly display its outwards- protruding bill. Regularly associated with the slang term "capping", meaning "lying". Responding to a message with a single 🧢 emoji is viewable as an accusation of lying (“cap”) while stating "no 🧢" ("no cap") is intended to emphasize the truthfulness of a statement.
Billed Cap was approved as part of Unicode 10.0 in 2017 and added to Emoji 5.0 in 2017.

name: Bird
description: A generic bird. Variously depicted as a blue or red bird, as a bluebird or cardinal, shown standing in full profile, or as a bird head. Both designs show the bird facing left. May be used for a variety of wild and pet birds as well as for metaphorical senses of bird (e.g., birdie in golf ). Apple and WhatsApp’s designs feature a grayish bird head. Notably, WhatsApp’s version appears in the popular “Snake With a Party Hat” meme image. Google, Samsung, and Facebook’s designs suggest a bluebird, Microsoft and Twitter’s a cardinal. Google’s bird previously resembled a canary, Samsung’s was previously green, and Microsoft and Twitter’s birds were once blue.
Bird was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Birthday Cake
description: A frosted cake with lit candles, as presented for a birthday celebration. The style of cake widely varies across platforms, though it usually has white frosting and strawberries , Apple, Google, and Samsung's designs suggest a Japanese Christmas cake . Other vendors depict a chocolate, pink, and/or sponge cake. Can occasionally be used as a playful reference to a person's "buttocks," inspired by the slang term "cake."
Birthday Cake was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Black Bird
description: A bird with black feathers, typically shown either standing in full profile. Can be used to represent various black-feathered birds, such as crows, ravens, blackbirds, and more. Black-feathered birds have been associated with magic and the occult across many global cultures, often as an omen of bad tidings. Frequently associated with the Baltimore Ravens, an American football team. WhatsApp's design previously just depicted the bird's head.
The Black Bird emoji is a ZWJ sequence combining 🐦 Bird , Zero Width Joiner and Black Large Square . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Black Bird was added to Emoji 15.0 in 2022.

name: Black Cat
description: A black cat shown in full profile, often with its tail curling upward.
The Black Cat emoji is a ZWJ sequence combining 🐈 Cat , Zero Width Joiner and Black Large Square . These display as a single emoji on supported platforms.
Black Cat was added to Emoji 13.0 in 2020.

name: Black Heart
description: A heart shaded completely black. May be used to express morbidity, sorrow, or a form of dark humor, but despite the color remains most commonly used for love and affection . Additionally, as with the other color-based hearts, this emoji is often also used to express an affinity with or appreciation for various people, places, groups, objects, or ideas associated with the same color.
Black Heart was approved as part of Unicode 9.0 in 2016 and added to Emoji 3.0 in 2016.

name: Black Large Square
description: A square shown in the shade of black. May be used to represent anything black. When players of the word game Wordle share their results on social platforms the results are represented through a series of green , yellow , and black or white square emojis. This emoji can indicate that the player guessed an incorrect letter, i.e. a letter that is not present within the word.
Black Large Square was approved as part of Unicode 5.1 in 2008 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Black Nib
description: The silver nib of a fountain pen, which distributes ink onto a writing surface. Positioned at a 45° angle, with its tip at the lower left or right. Like 🖋️ Fountain Pen , commonly used for various content concerning writing, drawing, and signing (e.g., laws, deals, in sports). Several platforms, including Google, Microsoft, and Samsung, depict only a nib, sometimes ringed with gold. Other platforms, including Apple and Twitter, feature the same designs as their 🖋️ Fountain Pen , but with their tips angled to the lower right.
Black Nib was approved as part of Unicode 1.1 in 1993 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Blossom
description: A flower that has blossomed. Depicted as a flower with white or yellow petals, as a daisy, with a golden center. Commonly used for Valentine’s Day , Mother’s Day , and other special occasions. May be more generally used to convey such ideas as love, appreciation, and happiness. Also used as a yellow or white accent color. Not to be confused with 🌻 Sunflower or 🌸 Cherry Blossom , though their applications may overlap. Google's flower was once pink. Microsoft's was previously yellow, Samsung's white.
Blossom was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Blowfish
description: A blowfish ( puffer ), which puffs up and becomes spiky when alarmed. Depicted as an orange or brown blowfish in full profile facing left, with small fins, a white underside, and a round, spiky body, as if inflated. Called fugu in Japan, where it’s consumed as a delicacy. May be to represent a variety of fish (saltwater or freshwater), fishing , metaphorical senses of fish , and fish as food, as consumed in the form of 🍣 Sushi . Not to be confused with 🐟 Fish or 🐠 Tropical Fish , though their applications may overlap. See also 🎣 Fishing Pole . Google’s blowfish was previously blue, Microsoft’s yellow, and Facebook’s white.
Blowfish was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Boar
description: A boar, a hairy, wild pig with tusks. Generally depicted as the face of a brown boar, either facing left or looking straight ahead, with prominent tusks projecting from its lower jaw. WhatsApp’s design displays the animal in full profile, as Google , Microsoft , and Samsung previously did. Twitter's design features a cartoon-styled face looking forward, as did an early Facebook design. Not to be confused with 🐖 Pig or 🐷 Pig Face , though their applications may overlap. Available as an Apple Animoji .
Boar was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Bomb
description: A cartoon-styled bomb, depicted as a black ball with a burning fuse. Commonly used for various figurative bombs or explosions, e.g., slang bomb , a “home run” in baseball or softball ; "excellent" or "attractive." Sometimes applied in contexts of war, weapons, or violence. Earlier designs from SoftBank and au by KDDI animated the bomb as exploding .
Bomb was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Bookmark
description: A bookmark, as used to mark one's place in a book . Appearance varies across platforms, but generally depicted at a 45° angle as a thin, white or red strip with a decorative tie and design, such as flower or star . May be used for various content concerning reading, labeling, or tagging. May also represent bookmarks on an internet browser or on a social media platform like Twitter , Instagram or TikTok . WhatsApp’s bookmark is purple. Twitter’s design shows a red bookmark in a closed book, similar to previous designs from Microsoft . Twitter and Google’s designs previously featured a blue bookmark. Not to be confused with 🏷️ Label .
Bookmark was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Bookmark Tabs
description: Sheets of white, printed paper with variously colored tabs to bookmark important sections or indicate signature lines. Commonly used for content concerning various types of documents and writing. The number of pages and tabs vary, with Microsoft and Twitter’s designs featuring one page with a single, purple-colored tab. Facebook’s is printed with NDA , or nondisclosure agreement . Most platforms indicate text with dark lines. Apple’s design features an easter egg, addressed Dear Katie and signed Take care from J ohn Appleseed with the text of its 1997–2002 Crazy Ones / Think Different ad campaign: Here’s to the crazy ones. The misfits. The rebels. The troublemakers. The round pegs in the square holes. The ones who see things differently. They’re not fond of rules. You can quote them, disagree with them, glorify or vilify them. About the only thing you can’t do is ignore them. Because they change things. They push the human race forward. And while some may see them as the crazy ones, we see genius. Because the ones who are crazy enough to think that they can change the world, are the ones who do. Early designs from au by KDDI resemble 📃 Page With Curl . Not to be confused with 📄 Page Facing Up or other emojis featuring sheets of paper.
Bookmark Tabs was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

name: Bottle with Popping Cork
description: A green bottle of champagne or sparkling wine with its cork popping and its bubbly contents spraying from the neck. Used for a range of celebratory occasions, such as New Year's Eve , birthdays , weddings , or other life accomplishments. Most platforms also include a golden label on the bottle, though this is absent from Facebook's design. JoyPixels' label includes their logomark. The spray varies by platform, appearing as white foam, yellow liquid, or stylized bubbles.
Bottle with Popping Cork was approved as part of Unicode 8.0 in 2015 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.

description: A bowl with a silver spoon inside, as used to eat cereal or soup. Bowl color varies across platforms, as do contents, though most are empty. WhatsApp’s bowl contains tomato soup, while Google’s previously held breakfast cereal. Earlier designs from Microsoft and Facebook also included food in their bowls.
Bowl with Spoon was approved as part of Unicode 10.0 in 2017 and added to Emoji 5.0 in 2017.

designs.title: Apple (2017-2026)
designs.description: Used by Apple devices (iPhone, iPad, Mac) whenever emojis are displayed. Also used by Telegram messenger.

designs.title: Google Noto Color Emoji (2017-2025)
designs.description: Default emoji set for Android devices created by Google and used on devices by Google, Xiaomi, Oppo, Huawei, Sony, and many others.

designs.title: Samsung (2018-2026)
designs.description: Custom emoji set used on Samsung phones and tablets.

designs.title: Microsoft 3D Fluent (2025)
designs.description: Glossy, gradient-heavy versions of the Microsoft emoji set. Used within select platforms such as Word and PowerPoint within the Windows 11 23H2 update.

designs.title: Microsoft Teams (3D Animated) (2024)
designs.description: 3D animated versions of Microsoft’s Fluent emoji set, used Microsoft Teams for PC and Android.

designs.title: Microsoft (2017-2025)
designs.description: Initially used across Microsoft PCs, though Windows 11 uses the 3D Fluent set as of 2025. Windows 10’s final update was in May 2019.

designs.title: WhatsApp (2017-2026)
designs.description: Used on WhatsApp for Android and PC. WhatsApp on iOS/MacOS uses Apple designs.

designs.title: Twitter / X (2017-2026)
designs.description: Used on Twitter / X for PC. Also used by Discord, Roblox, and Mastodon. Twitter / X on iOS/MacOS uses Apple designs. Android devices use native emoji design as of early 2023.

designs.title: Facebook (2017-2025)
designs.description: Used on Facebook for Android and PC. Not used across Meta’s WhatsApp and Instagram platforms. Facebook on iOS/MacOS uses Apple designs.

designs.title: Huawei (2023-2024)
designs.description: Custom emoji set used on select Huawei phones and tablets.

designs.title: JoyPixels (2017-2025)
designs.description: A licensable emoji design set. Previously named EmojiOne.

designs.title: LG (2021)
designs.description: Custom emoji set used on LG devices. Discontinued between 2017 and 2020, replaced by Noto Color Emoji, but then revived in 2021 for LG’s final mobile device.

designs.title: Skype (2015)
designs.description: Animated emoji-adjacent designs used by the Skype platform.

designs.title: Twitter Emoji Stickers (2022)
designs.description: Highly-detailed emoji set used by Twitter’s Statuses feature and within the tweet image editor on Android devices.

designs.title: SerenityOS (2026)
designs.description: Custom emoji set used on the open-source SerenityOS.

designs.title: Toss Face (토스페이스) (2022-2023)
designs.description: A custom emoji design set used by Korean fintech platform Toss.

designs.title: Sony Playstation (2021)
designs.description: Used on PlayStation 5 and PlayStation 4 within the device’s messaging functionality.

designs.title: Noto Emoji Font (2022-2025)
designs.description: A minimalist, monochrome version of Google’s Noto Color Emoji designs.

designs.title: OpenMoji (2018-2025)
designs.description: A open-source emoji design set by the HfG Schwäbisch Gmünd (Design University) in Germany.

designs.title: Icons8 (2023)
designs.description: A licensable emoji design set.

designs.title: emojidex (2017)
designs.description: An open-source emoji design set consisting of user-submitted emoji designs.

designs.title: Emojipedia Sample Images (2017-2018)
designs.description: Sample emoji designs developed by Emojipedia for illustrative purposes.

name: Bowling
description: Ten-pin bowling emoji, showing a bowling ball and pins.
Bowling was approved as part of Unicode 6.0 in 2010 and added to Emoji 1.0 in 2015.
